title: Mitigate host memcpy storms with async staging eviction and prioritized GPU dispatch
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: We've observed recurring short-duration but high-amplitude host-side memcpy spikes ('memcpy storms') during high-concurrency prefill bursts. These cause CPU threadpool contention, scheduler thrashing, and elevated p99 latencies for short to medium sequence workloads. Root causes appear to be: (1) synchronous eviction of staging buffers triggered by cache pressure, (2) unpredictable ordering of host->GPU dispatch that amplifies concurrent DMA submissions, and (3) worker thread oversubscription during prefill decode handoff.

Proposal: Implement an asynchronous staging eviction daemon combined with a prioritized GPU dispatch queue and a lightweight admission controller for prefill workers. Key components: 
- Async staging eviction: background worker that evicts least-recently-used staging slabs in bounded batches to smooth DMA bursts; eviction work is posted to a dedicated low-priority thread with backoff windows.
- Prioritized GPU dispatch: a small priority queue that favors in-flight decode continuations and short-sequence prefill completions (latency-sensitive) over long-running batched requests (throughput-oriented).
- Prefill admission controller: token-bucket style limiter per host core grouping to avoid sudden worker ramp-ups; integrates with console SLO signals to temporarily throttle non-critical traffic.
- Kernel selector hinting: when eviction is in-progress, preferentially select kernels with lower host-copy overhead (e.g., fused-kernel preference, half-precision memcpy-friendly kernels).

Expected benefits: reduce short-term memcpy peak IO, lower host thread contention, improve p50/p95 latencies for common PLG workloads, and keep throughput stable for long-running batches.

Design trade-offs and constraints: 
- Complexity: introduces a new eviction daemon and another queueing layer; needs careful instrumentation to avoid starvation.
- Memory usage: async eviction keeps some extra staging capacity reserved, slightly increasing host memory footprint under low pressure.
- Compatibility: prioritized dispatch must interoperate with existing kernel routing and fallback policies.

Acceptance criteria: 
1) p99 prefill latency for short sequences (<=64 tokens) decreases by >=10% under 95th percentile load test.
2) host CPU utilization 95th percentile decreases by >=15% during synthetic memcpy-burst tests.
3) No regression (>2%) in steady-state throughput for batched long sequences.
4) Rollout toggle available in runtime config and console.

Monitoring and dashboards: Add charts for per-host memcpy bytes/sec, staging-eviction-rate, dispatch-priority-queuesize, prefill-admission-rejections, and per-kernel host-copy time. Create alert if dispatch queue starvation persists >5m.

Rollout plan: Canary on 5 dedicated nodes (dev-dedicated-1..5) -> monitor 48h -> expand to 25% traffic -> full fleet. Rollback: toggle off daemon + revert kernel hinting; commit id pinned in rollout playbook.

Artifacts: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/async-staging-eviction, perf harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4127, initial perf report: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1xEvictPerf
comments: 2025-01-21 - Maya Chen: Initial triage notes. Observed memcpy spikes during tenanted prefill stress tests. Logged heap snapshots and DMA submission traces. Added as spike investigation task.

2025-01-24 - Diego Alvarez: Proof-of-concept async-evict thread implemented. Local microbench: memcpy peak amplitude reduced ~28% under synthetic workload. Need integration with admission controller and prioritized queue.
2025-01-28 - Sana Patel (PM): Confirmed customer reports align with synthetic test shape. Prioritize short-sequence latency wins for PLG onboarding flows. Approved P1 scope.

2025-01-30 - Liam O'Rourke (SR): Reviewed kernel hinting changes. Concern: can bias kernel selector too aggressively and harm long-batch throughput. Added canary metrics and guardrails (selector soft-hints, fallback after 3 failed dispatches).

2025-02-02 - Diego Alvarez: Integration PR opened (runtime#4127). CI perf tests attached; short-seq p50 improved 18%, p99 improved 12% on canary harness. Pushing for dev-dedicated canary today. See PR for microbench details.
2025-02-02 - Maya Chen: Added rollout checklist and monitoring dashboard links. Assigned follow-up tasks for QA and security review (low risk).
notes: Keep kernel-selector hints as soft preferences. If memcopy backlog > threshold, escalate to pick fused kernels; otherwise revert to throughput kernels. Coordinate with Dedicated infra for canary capacity.
implementation_plan: 1) merge async eviction daemon with config flag; 2) add prioritized dispatch queue and admission limits behind feature flag; 3) add kernel-selector soft-hints; 4) run canary and collect metrics; 5) progressive rollout with dashboard gating.
qa_steps: Run synthetic memcpy-burst test (tooling/perf/memstorm.py) at 10x baseline. Verify p50/p95/p99 and host CPU metrics. Run end-to-end regression with long-sequence throughput harness. Validate that eviction does not cause OOMs.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: starvation of low-priority throughput tasks. Mitigation: time-slice enforcement and automatic demotion/promotion policy. Risk: small memory footprint increase; mitigation: limit reserved staging to 5% host RAM and expose config.
implementation_notes: Use existing job-queue infra for dispatch priority to avoid new IPC paths. Eviction should use non-blocking free and post DMA ops in batched submissions (max batch 8). Ensure NUMA locality by pinning eviction worker to local core group.
release_notes_blurb: Reduced short-sequence latency by smoothing host memory-copy bursts. Feature is behind runtime-1.22 flag and will be gradually enabled for Dedicated nodes.
related_customers: AcmeChat, FastForms (reported increased onboarding latency during spikes)
estimated_cost_impact: small increase in host memory (~2-6% depending on workload) but lower token cost from fewer timeouts and retries.
communication_plan: Notify support and SRE channels before canary. Post canary summary to #runtime-telemetry with p50/p95/p99 charts and decision to proceed or rollback. Update public status page if customer impact is visible.
final_status_criteria: Merged PR + canary 48h stable + dashboard gates green + release note drafted
